title: Contiguous-aware KV allocator and lineage relocation for fragmentation mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Over time KV pools on GPUs fragment due to variable-length cache entries (context-dependent tokenization + different model architectures) and the continuous batching layer tends to allocate/deallocate many short-lived prefixes. This increases cold allocations during large fanout batches and forces expensive relocations that raise tail latency.

Goal: Implement a contiguous-aware allocator that reduces cross-batch fragmentation by placing hot, sequential KV ranges contiguously and introduce a lineage-based relocation mechanism to compact cold fragments with bounded pause. The solution should be aware of batch semantics (sequence-length distribution), provide throttled background compaction, and expose fragmentation telemetry to the Console.

Scope: Runtime allocator changes, batching hints API, background relocation controller, new telemetry metrics, integration tests and canary on dedicated nodes. Not in scope: changing model architectures or tokenizer formats.

Outcome metrics: reduce measurable fragmentation ratio by >= 40% on 95th percentile workloads, reduce relocation-induced tail latency spikes by >= 30%, keep per-request p99 latency regression < 5% during background compaction.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator places >= 70% of hot KV ranges contiguously as measured by our access-heatmap-based test harness
Background lineage relocation completes compaction windows with mean pause < 6ms and p99 < 25ms under normal load
Integration tests that simulate mixed batch sizes and long-running sessions show fragmentation ratio drop >= 40% compared to baseline
New telemetry emitted (fragmentation_ratio, reclaimable_bytes, relocation_ops/s, compaction_pause_ms) available in Console + exported to Prometheus
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-pool; rollback returns system to previous allocator without state corruption
implementation_plan: 1) Design allocator changes: introduce 'contiguous stride' allocations for hot token ranges + a small ephemeral pool for short-lived prefixes. Produce design doc and memory model diagrams (2d page) - owner: Rafael

2) Expose batch-hint API from batching layer to allocator: sequence_length_bucket and affinity_tag (string) so allocator can co-locate KV for same affinity. Minimal ABI change, backward compatible - owner: Priya

3) Implement lineage relocation controller: record lightweight relocation lineage per segment, perform copy-on-write relocations to contiguous regions, retire source segments asynchronously. Ensure relocations can be throttled by target latency SLOs - owner: Rafael

4) Add adaptive compaction window heuristic: widen when reclaimable_bytes high and narrow under high latency pressure. Use token-access heatmaps (recent 5m) to target cold fragments first - owner: Anshu
5) GPU-friendly copy kernels: implement batched memcpy kernels that overlap with async CUDA streams to hide relocation cost. Reuse existing kernel selection logic where possible - owner: Jae
6) Telemetry + Console hooks: new Prometheus exporters and Console dashboard panels showing fragmentation maps and cost impact - owner: Emma
7) Tests: unit allocator tests, stress harness simulating continuous batching, end-to-end on dedicated small cluster, and failure injection for mid-relocation crashes - owner: QA team
8) Canary rollout: enable on 10% of dedicated pools with runtime flag, run 72-hour stability and perf tests, then progressive increase - owner: SRE/Infra
telemetry: reclaimable_bytes: estimated contiguous bytes reclaimable without cross-lineage relocation
relocation_ops/s: number of relocation operations per second
compaction_pause_ms: histogram of pause times introduced by relocations
affinity_colocation_score: percent of affinity_tag allocations placed in same contiguous region
batch_coalescing_miss_rate: fraction of batch allocations that required remote KV fetches due to fragmentation
rollout_plan: Alpha: feature gate on internal dev cluster. Run synthetic workloads (short prefixes, mixed sequence lengths) and collect telemetry for 48h
Beta: enable on non-critical dedicated pools (10-20% traffic) for 72h, monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, relocation_ops and reclaimable_bytes
Canary: enable on 2 production pools with traffic routing, run for 7 days under normal traffic patterns
Full rollout: ramp to 50% then 100% after performance and stability gates pass; finalize Console dashboards and docs
Rollback: disable runtime flag and trigger safe retire path for partially relocated segments; verify integrity with consistency checker
risks: Relocation pause spikes under pathological workloads with very high churn - mitigated by adaptive throttle but still residual risk
Edge-case race where allocator's contiguous placement assumption conflicts with model-internal KV reuse patterns — will add per-model tuning knobs
GPU memcpy bandwidth could become a bottleneck during large-scale compaction; need to prioritize stream overlap and limit concurrency
Increased complexity in allocator makes debugging harder; we will add rich logging and a 'allocator-replay' mode to reproduce decisions
ABI change risk: batch-hint API needs strict backward compatibility testing with older runtime clients
